messages.subject: Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext()
parts:
Please help, 
Get an error about reactive function near this code:

stockstxtclosure <- reactive({
    query <- parseQueryString(clientData$url_search)
  
    stockstweets = searchTwitter(query[["ticker"]], n=10, lang="en")
    stockstxt = sapply(stockstweets, function(x) x$getText())
   
    return (stockstxt)
  })
  
  stockstxt = stockstxtclosure()
  
  stockstxt = gsub("(RT|via)((?:\\b\\W*@\\w+)+)", "", stockstxt)



Error is:
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext()
parts: Normally the answer is to put the offending call (stockstxtclosure()) in a proper reactive context, but in this case I'd take the code of stockstxtclosure out of a reactive expression and just call it directly. You'll get the same error then when you call clientData$url_search; change it to isolate(clientData$url_search) and you should be good to go.
